pairs.subject: migrations
pairs.evidence: crates/core/migrations/0004_simhash.sql:2 Existing records receive a zero sentinel without a chained backfill, leaving their derived fingerprints missing until a separate repair runs.

techniques.evidence: crates/core/migrations/0004_simhash.sql:2 No migration backfills existing fingerprints; the later reindex_simhashes utility requires separate execution, and migration 0020 documents the historical impact.

crates/core/migrations/0002_platform.sql:24 Datasets occupy rows in the fixed records table; searches of table creation and alteration statements found no operator-defined physical table set requiring migration discovery.
crates/core/src/storage.rs:607 allow_schema_ahead explicitly permits boot against newer ledger versions, violating mandatory downgrade refusal; ordinary migration errors otherwise propagate.
docs/deployment.md:55 The documented deployment forbids sharing the SQLite store between processes, so concurrent old and new application versions are outside the supported model.
crates/core/migrations/0006_watches.sql:4 The existence guard accepts any same-named table without verifying its intended shape, and the step has no live-schema postcondition.
crates/core/src/backup.rs:166 SQLite provides an in-store ledger with atomic step-and-marker writes; this context does not require markerless record-shape classification.
crates/core/src/backup.rs:231 After VACUUM INTO succeeds, backups are pruned and the path returned without opening or validating the new copy; readability is checked only in a test.
crates/core/src/storage.rs:623 The boot assertion compares table names only, allowing column, type, index, and trigger drift to pass despite the standard's schema-fingerprint requirement.

crates/core/migrations/0021_ingress.sql:43 The rebuild does not enumerate live dependents before dropping the table and recreates only idx_triggers_source, so operator-added indexes and SQL triggers would be lost.
